sentinel_issue: The observed room count reached 50,657 on 2026-09-03, nearly 10× the documented 5,120-room cap, and later remained 46,522–46,465; since new-file creation should fail closed past MAX_ROOMS, this indicates either a deployment/configuration mismatch or quota enforcement failure. This is a concrete disk-risk requiring verification of the live MAX_ROOMS setting and room-creation path.
worker_response: The data points to a live configuration mismatch, not proof of failed enforcement: 50,657 rooms were below the observed 81,920 capacity (16×5,120), and later 46,522 were below 163,840 (32×5,120), while capacities changed again to 250,000 on September 23/26. Verify the deployed MAX_ROOMS and creation-path response in the running container, then pin/reject unexpected values at startup (and add a metric exposing the effective cap); the ~10 MB top-room files show per-room compaction is working, but the 46k-room inventory still warrants immediate disk-budget measurement.
auditor_verdict: AGREE: The data shows room totals below the reported live capacities—50,657/81,920, 46,522/163,840, and 46,465/250,000—so it does not by itself prove quota-enforcement failure, but the capacity changes and reversion strongly support a configuration/deployment mismatch requiring verification. The roughly 8.6–10.4 MB top-room files do not establish compaction or eliminate aggregate disk risk from 46,465 rooms.
